title: S1 · E1 — The Flip
opening_question: No new metal. No extra pumping. So where does the extra heat come from?
answer_summary: Reversing one stream (counterflow) keeps the temperature difference — the driving force — alive along the whole tube, so every metre keeps transferring heat: about 36% more in the ideal single-pass case (equal heat-capacity rates, NTU = 2).
closing_question: But tubes don't stay clean. Next time — what a thin layer of grime does to all of this.
